pregnancy_by_week.10: You've reached 10 weeks, and your little one is now officially a fetus! This is a major milestone as all their essential organs have formed. Many people find their early pregnancy symptoms start to ease up around now.
pregnancy_by_week.11: Your baby is about the size of a fig, and tiny fingernails are starting to form. They're already moving around, but you probably won't feel it for a few more weeks.
pregnancy_by_week.12: You've reached the end of the first trimester! Your baby's reflexes are developing, and they can now open and close their hands and curl their toes.
pregnancy_by_week.13: Welcome to the second trimester! Many people find their energy levels start to return and morning sickness subsides. Your baby's vocal cords are now developing.
pregnancy_by_week.14: Your baby is starting to grow fine hair, called lanugo, all over their body, which helps keep them warm. They can also make facial expressions now, like squinting and frowning.
pregnancy_by_week.15: Your baby can now sense light. If you were to shine a flashlight on your belly, they might move away from the beam. Their taste buds are also forming.
pregnancy_by_week.16: Your baby's sensory development is kicking into high gear. They can now make sucking motions with their mouth, and their tiny ears are in their final position.
pregnancy_by_week.17: The skeleton is starting to harden from soft cartilage to bone. You might start feeling the first flutters of movement, often called 'quickening,' around this time!
pregnancy_by_week.18: Your baby's unique fingerprints and toe prints are now forming. Their nervous system is also maturing rapidly, allowing for more coordinated movements.
pregnancy_by_week.19: A waxy, protective coating called vernix caseosa is beginning to form on your baby's skin. This coating protects them from the amniotic fluid.
pregnancy_by_week.20: Congratulations, you're halfway there! The 20-week anatomy scan is often performed around this time. It's a great opportunity to discuss your baby's growth with your doctor.
pregnancy_by_week.21: Your baby is regularly swallowing amniotic fluid, which is great practice for their digestive system. You're likely feeling their kicks and jabs more consistently now.
pregnancy_by_week.22: Your baby now looks like a miniature newborn. Their senses of sight and hearing are continuing to improve, and they can even perceive your touch through the uterine wall.
pregnancy_by_week.23: Your baby's hearing is getting much better. They can now hear your heartbeat, your voice, and other sounds from outside. This is a perfect time to talk and sing to them!
pregnancy_by_week.24: A major milestone in lung development is happening this week as the branches of the respiratory 'tree' and surfactant production begin, making viability outside the womb a possibility.
pregnancy_by_week.25: Your baby is getting plumper as they gain more fat, which is making their skin less translucent. They may even be able to respond to your voice with movement.
pregnancy_by_week.26: At 26 weeks, your baby's eyes are starting to open and they are becoming more sensitive to sound. It's a good time to discuss the upcoming glucose screening test with your doctor.
pregnancy_by_week.27: You've reached the end of the second trimester! Your baby is practicing breathing by inhaling and exhaling amniotic fluid, and they may even have a regular sleep-wake cycle.
pregnancy_by_week.28: Welcome to the third trimester, the home stretch! Your baby's brain is developing rapidly, and they can now experience REM sleep, which means they might be dreaming.
pregnancy_by_week.29: Your baby is demanding a lot of nutrients, especially calcium for their hardening bones. This is a great time to focus on calcium-rich foods to support their growth.
pregnancy_by_week.30: Your baby is growing fast and gaining about half a pound a week from here on out. Their eyesight is continuing to develop, though their vision is still quite blurry.
pregnancy_by_week.31: All five of your baby's senses are now fully functional. They are busy processing information from all the sights, sounds, and tastes they are experiencing.
pregnancy_by_week.32: Your baby is likely getting into the head-down position in preparation for birth. Their skin is becoming soft and smooth as they continue to plump up.
pregnancy_by_week.33: Your baby's bones are hardening, but their skull remains soft and flexible. This allows the plates to overlap slightly, which helps them fit through the birth canal.
pregnancy_by_week.34: Your baby's lungs are nearly fully developed, and the protective vernix caseosa coating on their skin is getting thicker. They are getting ready for their big debut!
pregnancy_by_week.35: It's getting a bit crowded in there! Your baby doesn't have as much room to do somersaults, but you'll still feel plenty of strong kicks, jabs, and stretches.
pregnancy_by_week.36: Your baby may 'drop' into your pelvis around this time, a process called lightening or engagement. Be sure to discuss the signs of labor with your healthcare provider.
pregnancy_by_week.37: Congratulations, you've reached full term! This means your baby is developed enough to be born at any time from this week forward. Their lungs are mature and ready for the outside world.
pregnancy_by_week.38: Your baby is continuing to build a layer of fat to help them regulate their body temperature after birth. They are also shedding most of the fine lanugo hair that covered their body.
pregnancy_by_week.39: Your baby's brain is still developing at an incredible pace. It's one of the last organs to finish maturing, so every extra day inside helps them prepare for life outside.
pregnancy_by_week.40: You've reached your official due date! While this is the day everyone focuses on, remember that many babies arrive a little earlier or later. Don't worry if they're taking their time.
pregnancy_by_week.default: While I don't have a specific update for this week, development is happening every day! It's always best to discuss your baby's specific progress with your healthcare provider.

cycle_phases.menstruation: Your cycle has begun. It's a great time to focus on rest, gentle movement, and nourishing foods.
cycle_phases.follicular: As your energy returns after your period, you might find it's a great time for more active workouts.
cycle_phases.ovulation: You might be feeling a peak in your energy and mood around now. This is the fertile window of your cycle.
cycle_phases.luteal: As your body prepares for your next period, you might notice PMS symptoms. Gentle exercise and mindfulness can be very helpful now.
